key_insight: A physics-constrained neural-network strength function preserves phase-field strength accuracy at regularization lengths up to 10 times the Irwin characteristic length.
engineering_relevance: Decoupling strength fidelity from regularization length enables coarser meshes, reducing computational demands for fracture simulations of large structures.
method: Learn the material strength function directly from data using a physics-constrained neural network.
Incorporate the learned function into the phase-field crack-nucleation driving force.
Generalize calibration to multiple strength states and enforce openness in selected directions.
evidence_signal: One architecture fits four synthetic strength surfaces and experimental data for graphite and two rubbers; finite-element simulations validate the theory across fracture regimes.
watch_item: Reliable deployment still requires representative strength data and validation for the target material and loading conditions.
paper_title: Machine learning of strength surfaces enables high regularization length phase-field fracture
